1 thing to act on and 3 to keep an eye on.
kyles-nas · Mon 26 Oct 08:00 EDT to Mon 2 Nov 08:00 EST
1 thing to act on and 3 to keep an eye on.
ACT
Memory is too full.

What happened. It averaged 79% and peaked at 96% of 15.5 GB.

Why it matters. The stacks' memory limits already add up to more than the free RAM, so if both agents get busy at once the kernel kills a container to make room.

What to do. vault-claude uses the most memory (4.6 GB on average). Lower AGENT_MEM_LIMIT or RESEARCH_MEM_LIMIT in obsidian-vault/.env, move a service off the box, or add RAM.

WATCH
Monitoring was down for about 20 hours.

What happened. No samples from Tue 27 Oct 20:00 EDT to Wed 28 Oct 16:00 EDT. The NAS booted at Wed 28 Oct 15:35 EDT, so it was off or restarting during the gap that ended then.

Why it matters. Every number below covers 88% of the week, and anything that happened in the gaps is missing from them.

What to do. If you did not restart it, check QTS's System Logs for why: a power cut, a firmware update or a crash.

WATCH
The data volume will be full in about 90 days.

What happened. It grew 10.0 GB a day over the last 30 days, and has 900 GB free.

Why it matters. At that rate it fills around 31 Jan 2027.

What to do. Find what grew before buying disks: the snapshot repo, the agents' scratch and Docker images are the likeliest places.

WATCH
Memory use is climbing.

What happened. It averaged 79% this week, against 58% over the prior 3.3 weeks.

Why it matters. A rise with no new service to explain it usually means something is leaking.

What to do. If you added a service, this is expected. If not, look at each container's memory history in the dashboard for the one that keeps growing.
